'''Giuseppe Mingione''' (born 28 August 1972) is an Italian [[mathematician]] who is active in the fields of [[partial differential equation]]s and [[calculus of variations]].

==Scientific activity==
Mingione received his Ph.D. in mathematics from the [[University of Naples Federico II]] in 1999 having [[Nicola Fusco]] as advisor; he is professor of mathematics at the [[University of Parma]]. He has mainly worked on regularity aspects of the Calculus of Variations, solving a few longstanding questions about the [[Hausdorff dimension]] of the singular sets of minimisers of vectorial integral functionals and the boundary singularities of solutions to [[Elliptic partial differential equation|nonlinear elliptic systems]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Regularity of minima: an invitation to the Dark Side of the Calculus of Variations|url=http://dml.cz/bitstream/handle/10338.dmlcz/134645/AplMat_51-2006-4_4.pdf|publisher=Applications of Mathematics|access-date=May 6, 2013}}</ref> This connects to the work of authors as [[Frederick J. Almgren, Jr.|Almgren]], [[Ennio De Giorgi|De Giorgi]], [[Charles B. Morrey, Jr.|Morrey]], [[Enrico Giusti|Giusti]], who proved theorems asserting regularity of solutions outside a singular set (i.e. a closed subset of [[Null set|null measure]]) both in [[geometric measure theory]] and for variational systems of partial differential equations. These are indeed called partial regularity results and one of the main issues is to establish whether the dimension of the singular set is strictly less than the ambient dimension. This question found a positive answer for general integral functionals, thanks to the work of [[Jan Kristensen|Kristensen]] and Mingione, who also gave explicit estimates for the dimension of the singular sets of minimisers.<ref>{{cite journal|title=The singular set of minima of integral functionals|journal=[[Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis]]|volume=180|issue=3|pages=331–398|doi=10.1007/s00205-005-0402-5|bibcode=2006ArRMA.180..331K|year=2006|last1=Kristensen|first1=Jan|last2=Mingione|first2=Giuseppe|s2cid=121550836}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=The singular set of Lipschitzian minima of multiple integrals|journal=[[Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis]]|volume=184|issue=2|pages=341–369|doi=10.1007/s00205-006-0036-2|bibcode=2007ArRMA.184..341K|year=2007|last1=Kristensen|first1=Jan|last2=Mingione|first2=Giuseppe|s2cid=15872181}}</ref> Mingione also worked on nonlinear [[potential theory]] obtaining potential estimates for solutions to nonlinear elliptic and [[Parabolic partial differential equation|parabolic equations]]. Such estimates allow to give a unified approach to the regularity theory of quasilinear, degenerate equations<ref>{{cite web|title=Caccioppoli prize citation|url=http://umi.dm.unibo.it/caccioppoli/vincitori-en.html#2010|publisher=Italian Mathematical Union|access-date=May 5, 2013|archive-date=October 11, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171011071928/http://umi.dm.unibo.it/caccioppoli/vincitori-en.html#2010|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Nonlinear aspects of Calderón-Zygmund theory|journal=Jahresbericht der Deutschen Mathematiker-Vereinigung|volume=112|issue=3|pages=159–191|doi=10.1365/s13291-010-0004-5|year=2010|last1=Mingione|first1=Giuseppe|s2cid=120017610}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Gradient potential estimates |journal=[[Journal of the European Mathematical Society]] |volume=13 |issue=2 |pages=249–486 |doi=10.4171/JEMS/258 |year=2011 |last1=Mingione |first1=Giuseppe |doi-access=free }}</ref> and relate to and upgrade previous work of Kilpeläinen, Malý, [[Neil Trudinger|Trudinger]], [[Xu-Jia Wang|Wang]]. Together with [[Cristiana De Filippis]], Mingione proved a Schauder type theory for nonuniformly elliptic equations and functionals.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Nonuniformly Elliptic Schauder Theory|journal=[[Inventiones Mathematicae]]|volume=234|issue=3|pages=1109–1196|doi=10.1007/s00222-023-01216-2|year=2023|last1=De Filippis|first1=Cristiana|last2=Mingione|first2=Giuseppe|doi-access=free|arxiv=2201.07369|bibcode=2023InMat.234.1109D }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Regularity for Double Phase Problems at Nearly Filippis|first1=Cristiana|last2=Mingione|first2=Giuseppe|article-number=85 |doi-access=free|arxiv=2308.10222|bibcode=2023ArRMA.247...85D }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=The sharp growth rate in ==Recognition==
Mingione was awarded the 2005 [[Bartolozzi Prize]], the 2006 [[Stampacchia Medal]], the 2010 [[Caccioppoli Prize]] and the  2016  [[:it:Premio Amerio|Amerio Prize]]. In 2007 he was awarded an [[European Research Council|ERC]] grant.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vectorial Problems|url=https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/207573|publisher=European Research Council|access-date=August 6, 2024}}</ref> Mingione is listed as an [[ISI highly cited researcher]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Lists of ISI highly cited researchers|url=https://clarivate.com/hcr/researchers-list/archived-lists/|access-date=2018-03-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180526092507/https://clarivate.com/hcr/researchers-list/archived-lists/|archive-date=2018-05-26|url-status=dead}}</ref> and was invited to deliver the  [[ETH Zurich|ETH]] Zürich Nachdiplom Lectures in 2015.<ref>{{cite web|title=ETH Lectures in Mathematics|url=https://math.ethz.ch/fim/lectures/nachdiplom-lectures/past-lectures.html/|access-date=2019-08-19|archive-date=2019-08-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190819225513/https://math.ethz.ch/fim/lectures/nachdiplom-lectures/past-lectures.html/|url-status=dead}}</ref>.He was invited speaker at the 2016 [[European Congress of Mathematics]] in Berlin.<ref>{{cite web|title=List of speakers at the 2016 ECM|url=http://www.7ecm.de/program/speakers.html}}</ref> In 2017 he was appointed Commander of the [[Order of Merit of the Italian Republic]] by the [[President of Italy|President]] of the [[Italian Republic]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Prof. Giuseppe Mingione, Commander|url=https://www.quirinale.it/onorificenze/insigniti/342345}}</ref>
